As we now have section HTTP Message Structure Validation, then I think requirement V15.3.8 matches better to this section compared to more abstract Defensive Coding:
| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **15.3.8** | Verify that, if the application (backend or frontend) builds and sends requests, it uses validation, sanitization, or other mechanisms to avoid creating URIs (such as for API calls) or HTTP request header fields (such as Authorization or Cookie), which are too long to be accepted by the receiving component. This could cause a denial of service, such as when sending an overly long request (e.g. a long cookie header field) results in the server always responding with an error status. | 3 | v5.0.be-10.4.9 |

So the proposal is to move 15.3.8 to section V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation

Also 2 grammar fixes for the requirement:
> Verify that, if the application (backend or frontend) builds and sends requests, it uses validation, sanitization, or other mechanisms to avoid creating URIs (such as for API calls) or HTTP request header fields (such as Authorization or Cookie), which are too long to be accepted by the receiving component.
